definitions.explanation: The act of detecting or identifying something, typically by a sensor, device, or system. Often used in technical contexts for automated detection of substances, signals, or conditions.

examples.japanese: ガス{漏|も}れを{検知|けんち}する。
センサーが{異常|いじょう}な{温度|おんど}を{検知|けんち}した。
examples.english: The sensor detected an abnormal temperature.

examples.japanese: この{装置|そうち}は{微量|びりょう}の{有害|ゆうがい}ガスでも{検知|けんち}できる{性能|せいのう}を{持|も}っている。
examples.english: This device has the capability to detect even trace amounts of harmful gas.

notes: Often used with する to form the verb {検知|けんち}する (to detect). Common collocations: {検知|けんち}{器|き} (detector), {検知|けんち}センサー (detection sensor), {検知|けんち}{能力|のうりょく} (detection capability). Used primarily in technical and scientific contexts. Related: {検出|けんしゅつ} (detection — often used for laboratory analysis), {感知|かんち} (sensing — more general, includes human perception), {探知|たんち} (detection — often for searching/locating).
